The recorder's `on_log(self, args, state, control, logs=None, **kwargs)` will therefore receive ONLY the trainer's built-in log scalars (loss, lr, grad_norm) and NEVER any `marker_band_stop/*` keys.

Concrete consequence:

### 1. Push the marker implant past emission onset to test whether per-context singleton structure emerges with stronger training — Diagnostic

**Parent:** #527
**Goal:** Test whether pushing the marker implant past emission onset (source log P(marker) − base in the [14, 20] nat window where on-policy emission begins) makes the per-context singleton shifts develop effective rank ≥ 2 across held-out contexts, so that the additivity-cosine read becomes a diagnostic superposition test rather than a measurement of constant-direction steering.

**Hypothesis:** The rank-1 collapse of singleton shifts at the [5, 7.5] nat band-stop is a property of the early ramp regime — the model satisfies the marker-only loss with a constant steering direction at low log-prob delta but, as training pushes log P(marker) past the EOS crossover (~step 60-100 per marker-training-recipe.md), it has to differentiate which contexts emit the marker, so the per-context structure of singleton shifts grows (singleton effective rank rises above 2.0; GD3 passes). If GD3 passes at the harder dial point, the additivity-cosine DV1 read becomes structurally diagnostic and grades either pass-or-fail on the rank-one-map-plus-beacons additivity pillar.

**Falsification:** Singleton effective rank stays ≤ 2.0 at the harder dial point (GD3 still fails uniformly), and the joint matrix top-1 SV share stays > 0.75 (GD1 still fails).
